newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mostly up on exports, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mostly up on exports, technicals.

text.p: CBOT soybeans closed mostly higher, led by nearby January, on active exports, tight nearby cash supplies and slow farmer selling, traders said.
Technical indicators which remain supportive for the long-term also boosted prices, they said.
"The market found good support at the day's lows and came back. The Dow was coming back which may have helped some," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
The Dow fell 50 points early, triggering index-arbitrage trading curbs on the New York Stock Exchange. The Dow then recouped a portion of the early losses.
January soybeans fluctuated between first support at $7.05 and first resistance at $7.13 per bushel. The day's low for January was $7.05-3/4 and the high was $7.13-1/2.
"It was a good close in beans even though we didn't take out yesterday's (Monday) highs of $7.15. We go through that and we could get to $7.23 pretty quick," a technician said.
Refco Inc was a later buyer of one million January.
Soybeans closed five cents per bushel higher to two lower, with January up five at $7.13.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 45,000 contracts, below the 49,357 traded Monday, according to the CBOT.
In soybean options, Cargill Investor Services bought 300 January $7.25 calls at four cents and Iowa Grain bought 200 May $7.25 puts at 40 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 11,000 contracts, above the 10,024 traded Monday.
